subject: Problem getting confidence limits with covariates

messages.author: 12cad5a425e186dd
messages.subject: Problem getting confidence limits with covariates
parts:
Hi,

I have this very simple test data set:
> uftest
  y.1 y.2 y.3  sp
1   0   1   0  Lu
2   0   0   0  Lu
3   1   1   1  Lu
4   1   1   0 Jor
5   0   1   0 Jor
6   1   1   1 Jor

These are 3x3 presence/absence matrices for two species at three sites followed during three time periods, so I am using species as a site covariate.

I fitted the following model:

> resfull<-occu(~sp ~sp,data=uftest)

So this model will give me species-specific parameters for occupancy and det. Prob.

Now, I want to find confidence limits for the detProb of each of these species, so tried this, but gives me an error:

> lc<- linearComb(resfull,coefficients=c(Intercept=1,sp="Lu"),type="det")
Error in function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function "linearComb", for signature "unmarkedFitOccu", "character"

It works if I put 0,1,2 etc in sp= , but not sure which species I am testing. Am I missing something here? (sorry, still figuring out the package).

Thanks,

Jorge
--

Technical Director

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Problem getting confidence limits with covariates
parts:
Hi Jorge,

In this case, the coefficients argument should be a dummy variable. I
think this should work:

backTransform(linearComb(resfull,coefficients=c(1, 0), type="det")) #
This will be p for the species coded as the reference level by R
backTransform(linearComb(resfull,coefficients=c(1, 1), type="det")) #
This will be p for the other species

An alternative is to use predict. Try this:

newdf <- data.frame(sp=factor(c("Lu", "Jor")))
predict(resfull, newdata=newdf, type="det")


Let us know if it works out.

Richard

That's odd. Look what I get:


umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(
y = matrix(c(0,0,1,1,0,1,1,0,1,1,1,1,0,0,1,0,0,1), 6, 3),
siteCovs = data.frame(sp = factor(c("Lu","Lu","Lu","Jor","Jor","Jor"))))

fm <- occu(~sp ~sp, umf)
nd <- data.frame(sp=factor(c("Lu", "Jor")))
predict(fm, newdata=nd, type="det", appendData=TRUE)

Predicted SE lower upper sp
1 0.6340457 0.2241376 0.2069072 0.9200403 Lu
2 0.6666958 0.1571314 0.3334425 0.8888663 Jor

What do other people get if they run this example?

Richard
